intervention_label: SDHA germline panel + SDHA/SDHB IHC re-cut with internal control + tumor-tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants (one-tissue-pull, three-answers diagnostic gate)
expected_benefit: Resolves three load-bearing diagnostic questions in one tissue pull: (1) is SDHA L306P germline (cascade testing + lifetime PGL surveillance) or somatic (biallelic somatic loss); (2) does SDHA IHC loss reconcile the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic paradox so the dSDH-GIST label survives a trial-screener review; (3) are PIK3CA R93W, MAP2K1 P124S, and SDHA E350fs clonal in tumor or ctDNA-only artifacts. Decisive for enrollment on the three dSDH-GIST trials (belzutifan NCT04924075, temozolomide NCT05661643, pemigatinib NCT07434843), all of which use SDHB-IHC loss as the entry phenotype.
key_risks: No therapeutic toxicity — germline blood draw + IHC re-cut on existing FFPE + comprehensive NGS panel
Adds 2-4 weeks of turnaround before any trial-route contingency conversation can move forward

If SDHA IHC also reads as intact after a clean re-stain, the dSDH-GIST label collapses and the trial-route options foreclose; the case becomes a molecularly-SDH-deficient / immunohistochemically-SDH-proficient outlier
preference_alignment: matches user's prefers_trials default: YES (every dSDH-GIST trial requires SDHB-IHC loss + confirmed driver); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (no therapeutic effect; gates the trial-route contingency stack)
guideline_status: Standard SDHx workup per the 2025 Florou review (pmid:39927693) and Endocrine Society 2014 PPGL guideline; SDHA IHC orthogonal arbitration per Miettinen 2013 (pmid:23023976) and Wagner 2013 (pmid:23459398).
rationale_summary: All five personas converged on this row. The biallelic SDHA inactivation call (combined VAF ~85%) should destabilize the SDH complex and abolish SDHB staining; the report says SDHB IHC is intact, and that discrepancy is the load-bearing diagnostic flag in the entire case. The critic framed it most sharply (rank 2): every dSDH-GIST trial entry phenotype runs through SDHB-IHC loss, so the IHC discordance is not a footnote, it is a structural threat to the trial-portfolio eligibility. The advocate ranked the bundle at 3 and named the operational discipline (one tissue pull, three answers). The conservative endorsed the diagnostic gating in round 2 and added that every dollar of chronic-toxicity exposure averted by NOT anchoring a PI3Kα or MEK inhibitor on an unconfirmed ctDNA-only call is a clean win. The germline SDHA result also drives the cascade-testing conversation for first-degree relatives and locks in the lifetime PGL-surveillance program; the SDHA IHC arbitrates whether this is SDHA-driven dSDH-GIST (locked in regardless of SDHB stain) or a non-SDHA SDHx driver where SDHC promoter methylation is the next fallback call.
open_questions: If SDHB remains intact after a clean re-stain with positive internal control and SDHA IHC is also retained, the next call is SDHC promoter methylation (research/academic referral, 4-8 weeks)
Whether the PIK3CA R93W and MAP2K1 P124S ctDNA calls confirm in tissue — if not, the PI3Kα and MEK inhibitor pathways drop out entirely
Germline SDHA cascade-testing conversation should wait for the panel result (2-3 weeks) before family discussions begin
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty — locks the dSDH-GIST driver call, resolves the SDHB-intact paradox, and gates the three dSDH-GIST trials at recurrence.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — germline blood draw + IHC re-cut on archival FFPE + comprehensive tumor NGS panel)

overall: Non-therapeutic workup that resolves the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic paradox and locks in trial-screener eligibility before any contingency is reached for.

intervention_label: Active surveillance — structured cross-sectional imaging q3-6 months for 2-3 years then space out, no adjuvant systemic therapy
expected_benefit: Preserves every downstream option. The natural history (Mei 2018 NIH 76-pt cohort, median EFS ~2.5 years post-R0, ~71% eventual recurrence) supports imaging surveillance over a regimen the molecular evidence rejects. Boikos 2016 (pmid:27011036) anchors the empirical 'no' on adjuvant imatinib: 1/49 (2%) PR in dSDH-GIST on imatinib vs 7/38 (18%) on sunitinib, with imatinib effectively inactive in this molecular subset.
key_risks: Indefinite scan-based follow-up is a real soft cost — patient anxiety burden is not captured in any toxicity table
PGL imaging carries cumulative radiation if CT-based; whole-body MRI as backbone mitigates

Multifocal primary plus resected M1 deposit puts this patient outside the cleanest published natural-history cohorts (mostly localized primaries) — the 2.5-year mEFS estimate is a floor, not a ceiling
Surveillance interval in dSDH-GIST is consensus-derived rather than RCT-supported
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: YES (no chronic toxicity committed for a low-yield mechanism in NED disease); matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: PARTIAL (registry enrollment at rank 3 satisfies the trial-preference axis; surveillance itself is not a trial)
guideline_status: NCCN GIST v1.2025 and ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 both explicitly recommend AGAINST adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST. Cross-society convergence on surveillance is unambiguous.
rationale_summary: Four of five personas put this at rank 1 (conservative, critic, concensusite, advocate); the risktaker did not rank surveillance but explicitly stated in their notes that the patient gets no adjuvant systemic therapy, which is the same call by another name. The concensusite framed the cross-society convergence most cleanly: NCCN GIST v1.2025 and ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 both recommend against adjuvant imatinib in dSDH-GIST. The advocate added the option-preservation argument: starting an adjuvant TKI now would burn screening eligibility for several trial-route contingencies (most require measurable disease and deprioritize prior-systemic-therapy patients). The conservative anchored the toxicity-side argument: even if Z9001/SSGXVIII/PERSIST-5 data transported (they don't — dSDH-GIST was not represented), the imatinib 3-year AE profile (G2+ edema ~30%, fatigue ~50%, hepatic/cardiac monitoring burden) would still fail the NED-patient toxicity threshold at a 2% PR rate. The advocate's round-2 critique on the conservative pick added a discipline note: the surveillance plan should bundle the registry + PGL screen + Signatera + imaging cadence as one active-surveillance package rather than reading as passivity. Preferences are defaulted — a real elicitation should happen before this hardens, but the toxicity math gets to the same answer under any plausible weight when there is no efficacy signal to lean on for an adjuvant regimen.
open_questions: Patient geography and travel tolerance — not specified in preferences.json; relevant to registry enrollment and trial-route contingencies at recurrence
Scan-anxiety tolerance — the soft cost of indefinite imaging-based follow-up is a real preference axis nobody has elicited yet
Whether surveillance should run on CT (cumulative-radiation cost) or whole-body MRI (payer-auth burden) as the backbone modality
likelihood_of_effect: Effect is option preservation. Cross-society guideline convergence + Boikos 2016 (1/49 PR on imatinib) close the door on adjuvant systemic therapy in this molecular subset.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — imaging surveillance has no AE profile; soft cost is scan anxiety, not characterized in any toxicity table)

counter_productive_moa.description: Non-therapeutic management pathway — no mechanism-level risk to a therapeutic goal.

overall: The right answer today and the call cross-society guidelines explicitly make; every contingency below this row depends on not burning option space now.

intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study enrollment (NCT03739827) + cancer-genetics counseling referral covering SDHA germline result and POLE R1679C reclassification
expected_benefit: Zero-toxicity intervention with the highest yield-per-cost in the dossier. Registry enrollment is open regardless of disease status (NED post-R0 is not a blocker), gives the patient longitudinal specialty follow-up at the NIH Pediatric & wild-type GIST Clinic, opens access to SDHC promoter methylation testing if the SDHA workup collapses, and seeds biospecimen banking that pays forward if a trial slot opens at recurrence. Pairs naturally with cancer-genetics counseling once the germline SDHA panel returns; POLE R1679C lands on the VUS side of the ledger (outside the canonical proofreading hotspots, TMB <1, MSS), so the counseling visit closes that loose end rather than triggering polyposis surveillance.
key_risks: Requires one in-person baseline visit at NIH Bethesda (or OHSU / Texas Children's) — travel is the operational cost
Germline SDHA result returns in 2-3 weeks; cascade-testing conversation with first-degree relatives should wait for the result
POLE counseling will most likely land on VUS — the patient should be told upfront so the result is not over-interpreted
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: YES (only trial the patient can join today — no measurable-disease requirement, no investigational drug); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: YES (zero toxicity, infrastructure for every downstream option)
guideline_status: Endocrine Society 2014 PPGL screening guideline (endorsed by ESMO and ENS@T) points at NCI Pediatric & wt-GIST Clinic as the reference center for SDHx-deficient cases; registry enrollment is the entry door.
rationale_summary: All five personas surfaced this as the highest-yield zero-toxicity move. Conservative and concensusite ranked it at 2, advocate at 2, risktaker at 5 (still endorsing the access logic), and the critic endorsed it in round 2 on conservative's pick. Three structural arguments converged: (1) the patient is NED so most contingency trials are inaccessible by measurable-disease requirements, but the registry is not; (2) the SDHC promoter methylation fallback assay is essentially unavailable outside academic referral channels and the NIH wt-GIST clinic is the most accessible US path; (3) biospecimen banking now pays forward if a slot on PEMIGIST or LITESPARK-015 opens at recurrence. The critic's round-2 push was that the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic discrepancy should be elevated more sharply than the conservative's rank-2 framing did — it is the load-bearing diagnostic threat to every trial-route contingency, not one of several loose ends. Cancer-genetics counseling pairs with the germline SDHA result and folds the POLE R1679C VUS framing into one coherent family-risk discussion rather than two staggered ones.
open_questions: Whether the patient's geography supports the NIH baseline visit (or whether OHSU / Texas Children's is the better operational fit)
Whether the SDHA germline panel will return in time to inform the in-person registry visit or whether the visit should run first
Whether the cancer-genetics counselor's preferred sequencing is germline panel first or counseling visit first

toxicity_burden: Low (none — registry enrollment + counseling visit; one in-person NIH baseline)

counter_productive_moa.description: Infrastructure, not therapy — no mechanism-level risk to a therapeutic goal.

overall: The highest yield-per-cost move on the page — zero-toxicity registry access plus genetics counseling that unlocks every downstream option.

intervention_label: Paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma baseline surveillance — plasma free metanephrines (LC-MS/MS) + rapid-sequence whole-body MRI; Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT reserved for baseline + change-flagging
expected_benefit: Patient-safety floor for an SDHx carrier and a one-time setup cost. An unscreened functional paraganglioma in an SDHx carrier going to anesthesia for any reason is a hypertensive-crisis hazard — directly relevant given the possibility of future re-operation if the patient recurs. Plasma free metanephrines by LC-MS/MS is the reference-standard biochemical screen; whole-body MRI is the repeatable imaging backbone; Ga-68 DOTATATE is the most sensitive functional tracer for SDHx-driven PGL but adds radiation and is unevenly available at community centers.
key_risks: Whole-body MRI sometimes requires prior auth even with documented SDHx-carrier indication
Ga-68 DOTATATE coverage is uneven outside NCI-designated centers with NET programs
If the SDHA germline result returns negative (somatic-only), the lifetime PGL surveillance cadence relaxes; biennial-vs-annual cadence depends on that result
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: YES (non-invasive imaging + blood draw); no preference conflicts elicited or apparent
guideline_status: Endocrine Society 2014 Pheochromocytoma/Paraganglioma guideline (endorsed by ESMO and ENS@T) is explicit on biochemical screening + baseline whole-body MRI in SDHx carriers.
rationale_summary: The advocate ranked PGL screening explicitly at rank 4; the concensusite folded it into the rank-2 registry+screening package; the conservative built it into the rank-1 surveillance plan; the critic anchored it on Endocrine Society 2014. All four named-endorse personas converge on the same workup; the risktaker did not rank it separately. The advocate framed the operational value most clearly: one whole-body MRI plus one plasma metanephrines draw establishes the clean baseline now, so the question at any later point becomes 'what has changed' rather than 'do we have a baseline.' The cadence decision (biennial vs annual, MRI-only vs DOTATATE-augmented) ties to the SDHA germline result — a confirmed germline carrier triggers the lifelong biennial-imaging cadence; a fully somatic case has lower extra-GIST cancer risk and the schedule shifts. Defer the DOTATATE follow-on to baseline + change-flagging to limit cumulative radiation.
open_questions: Whether the treating center's nuclear-medicine program runs Ga-68 DOTATATE on-site (generator dependence) or whether a referral is needed
Whether to bundle the metanephrines draw with the germline SDHA blood draw — operationally efficient, separate result paths
likelihood_of_effect: Patient-safety floor — establishes clean PGL/PCC baseline and the anesthesia-safety screen required before any future elective surgery in an SDHx carrier.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — imaging + blood draw; minimal radiation if MRI-first, DOTATATE deferred)

counter_productive_moa.description: Non-therapeutic surveillance — no mechanism-level risk to a therapeutic goal.

overall: Standard SDHx-carrier surveillance — anesthesia-safety floor and a clean comparator baseline for the recurrence-monitoring strategy.

expected_benefit: The patient has ctDNA-detectable SDHA E350fs plus PIK3CA and MAP2K1 variants pre-resection, so plasma is informative in this individual. Signatera can build a bespoke panel from those variants for serial MRD tracking. Tumor-informed assays give a lead-time signal ahead of cross-sectional imaging in colorectal and lung post-resection settings; GIST-specific prospective validation is thinner.
key_risks: GIST has weaker prospective MRD validation than colorectal or lung — frame as informative, not therapy-triggering
Signatera baseline build needs an FFPE block; coordinate with the SDHB IHC re-stain and tissue NGS confirmation orders to share tissue
A ctDNA-positive / imaging-negative result is a known counseling challenge — the response is shortened-interval imaging (6-8 weeks), NOT systemic-therapy initiation
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: PARTIAL (not a trial, but adjunct to the trial-aware surveillance plan); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: YES (no therapeutic toxicity; venipuncture only)
guideline_status: Not in NCCN or ESMO GIST guidelines as a standard surveillance tool; tumor-informed MRD has stronger validation in colorectal (Reinert 2019, Henriksen 2021) than in GIST.
rationale_summary: Conservative ranked this at 4, risktaker at 5, advocate at 3 (bundled with the SDHA workup). The critic echoed that discipline in round 2. The advocate's bundling of Signatera with the SDHA workup raised a similar tension — the rationale prose described ctDNA as something that 'could legitimately move the conversation from surveillance to sunitinib before the patient is symptomatic,' which the conservative correctly flagged as the actionable framing the validation data don't support. toxicity_burden: Low (none — venipuncture; FFPE block re-use for baseline build)

intervention_label: Sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4-on/2-off (or 37.5 mg continuous) — first systemic line at measurable recurrence; NOT adjuvant
expected_benefit: Best-characterized 2L systemic option for KIT/PDGFRA-WT GIST at recurrence. Demetri 2006 (Lancet, n=312, RoB2:Low) anchors the registration-grade efficacy + safety dataset: TTP HR 0.33 (p<0.0001), mTTP 27.3 wks vs 6.4 wks. The dSDH-specific signal runs through Boikos 2016 (pmid:27011036): 7/38 (18%) objective response in dSDH-GIST on sunitinib vs 1/49 (2%) on imatinib — directional, not a precise estimate (retrospective n=38, no CI, ROBINS-I:Moderate).
key_risks: Hand-foot skin reaction, hypothyroidism, fatigue, hypertension, skin discoloration — well-characterized class AEs with published management algorithms
Most dSDH-GIST patients need dose modification to 37.5 mg continuous within 2-3 cycles — plan for this as the rule rather than the exception (Mavroeidis 2025, Dedousis 2025)
Cumulative hypothyroidism risk rises with exposure duration; chronic monitoring needed but routine
dSDH-GIST patients tend to be younger and need multi-year TKI exposure if they respond — the natural-history timescale of the disease accumulates chronic AE burden
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: PARTIAL (FDA-approved, not a trial — the advocate flagged in round 2 that at recurrence sunitinib should be presented alongside the trial-route options rather than ahead of them as the default 2L); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: YES on the contingency framing (chronic AE profile is real but well-characterized)
guideline_status: NCCN GIST v1.2025 lists sunitinib as the preferred 2L TKI for KIT/PDGFRA-WT (including dSDH) GIST. ESMO 2022 concurs. The NCCN 2A endorsement rests on Boikos 2016 retrospective n=38 rather than RCT-level subset evidence — expert consensus on the best available data.
rationale_summary: Conservative, critic, and concensusite all ranked sunitinib at 3 with explicit 'NOT adjuvant today' framing; advocate placed it at 5 to formalize the contingency-only positioning. The risktaker dissented in their notes: at 18% ORR in dSDH-GIST, sunitinib is a fallback after the high-effect-size trial picks fail or close, not a primary play. Advocate's round-2 critique on the conservative and critic rank-3 placements flagged the same preference-fit tension: prefers_trials defaults to true, and at recurrence the sunitinib path should be presented alongside the trial route (PEMIGIST, LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST, NCT05661643 temozolomide) rather than ahead of it. The critic's round-2 push was a directional caveat: the Boikos 2016 18% ORR has no confidence interval and the dSDH subset in the Demetri 2006 pivotal phase 3 is minimally represented, so the activity claim runs through subgroup extrapolation, not subset-of-RCT evidence. Conservative's round-2 operational note: build 37.5 mg continuous into the contingency plan as the anticipated trajectory rather than treating it as a failure of label dosing.
open_questions: At the moment of recurrence, whether the trial-route options (PEMIGIST, LITESPARK-015, NCT05661643) should be evaluated alongside sunitinib rather than sequenced after it — the defaulted prefers_trials preference set raises the bar for the trial side
Whether the patient tolerates 50 mg 4-on/2-off or needs to start at 37.5 mg continuous
Whether to initiate on rising ctDNA alone or wait for RECIST-measurable disease (board consensus: imaging-measurable disease, not ctDNA-positive alone)
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate at first measurable recurrence — Boikos 2016 dSDH-GIST 18% ORR (n=38 retrospective, no CI); Demetri 2006 registration-grade 2L GIST (TTP HR 0.33).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (HFSR, hypothyroidism, fatigue, hypertension — well-characterized chronic class AEs; published management algorithms apply)

counter_productive_moa.description: Class-effect VEGFR signaling withdrawal on chronic dosing; no mechanism-level dissent for THIS subset in the board's deliberation.

overall: Best-characterized 2L TKI for KIT/PDGFRA-WT GIST; contingency-only at measurable recurrence, with the trial-route options as a co-equal conversation rather than a downstream fallback.

intervention_label: Belzutifan 120 mg PO daily on LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort (NCT04924075) — contingency at first measurable recurrence, gated on dSDH phenotype confirmation
expected_benefit: Mechanism case is the cleanest in this dossier: SDH loss raises intracellular succinate to mM concentrations and stabilizes HIF-2α (Selak 2005 pmid:15652751), and belzutifan binds the HIF-2α PAS-B pocket to block heterodimerization with ARNT. The closest mechanism-matched human readout is LITESPARK-015 PPGL cohort (ORR 26%, DCR 85%, mPFS 22 mo). 14 US sites recruiting. Wt-GIST cohort has no published readout yet — the bet is on cross-tumor mechanism transport from PPGL to dSDH-GIST.
key_risks: Hypoxia and anemia at the EPO-suppression target are dose-limiting in roughly 25-30% of treated patients in the broader belzutifan dataset

Roux-en-Y reconstruction compounds anemia management: iron and B12 absorption are compromised, and EPO suppression on top of that is a stacked hit — baseline Hgb/iron/B12 must be documented before enrollment
Post-marketing surveillance is in the ~5-year window since August 2021 VHL approval — at the low end of long-tail safety follow-up for a chronic oral

No published wt-GIST efficacy readout yet — the bet rides on cross-tumor mechanism transport that LITESPARK-015 may or may not validate; a negative wt-GIST cohort closes the modality entirely with no successor (DFF332 and NKT-2152 both discontinued 2025-2026)
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: YES (recruiting, 14 US sites); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (mechanism foundation strong, no GIST-specific efficacy signal yet); needs a real Roux-en-Y / Hgb / iron / B12 baseline conversation before enrollment given the post-gastrectomy anatomy
guideline_status: No NCCN or ESMO GIST listing. The guideline-fit case is the NCCN trial-enrollment principle for off-guideline targeted therapy.
rationale_summary: Risktaker rank 2, critic rank 5 (trial-watch), concensusite rank 5 (bundled with TMZ and pemigatinib), advocate implicit endorsement through 'preserves every future option' framing. Multiple round-2 qualifications stack but no formal dissent: conservative on toxicity (hypoxia/anemia in a Roux-en-Y patient is the stacked hit the rationale underweights), advocate on preference fit (real preferences elicitation required before this lands as a contingency), critic on evidence quality (PPGL ORR 26% does not transport quantitatively to GIST; single-arm open-label ORR endpoint will not generate OS evidence). The trial requires measurable disease and pathologist-confirmed dSDH phenotype — hence the conditional framing. With DFF332 (NCT04895748) terminated February 2026 and NKT-2152 discontinued, belzutifan is the sole active HIF-2α option — a negative wt-GIST readout would close the modality entirely. Watch for ASCO 2026 / WCGIC for the GIST-cohort interim cut.
open_questions: LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort interim readout (ASCO 2026 / WCGIC most likely)
Post-gastrectomy / Roux-en-Y belzutifan PK and anemia tolerability — not formally studied
Whether ctDNA pharmacodynamics (succinate-HIF-2 target genes) can be tracked on serial plasma for early-response assessment
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate if dSDH phenotype confirms — PPGL adjacency (ORR 26%, mPFS 22 mo) does not quantitatively transport to GIST; cleanest mechanism case but no GIST efficacy readout yet.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (anemia and hypoxia dose-limiting in 25-30% on broader dataset; stacked anemia management problem in Roux-en-Y; ~5-year post-marketing surveillance)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cross-tumor mechanism transport from PPGL to GIST is the gating uncertainty — modality-level risk, not patient-AE risk.

overall: Cleanest mechanism case for dSDH-GIST in the dossier — 14 US sites recruiting; cross-tumor transport from PPGL is the live question and Roux-en-Y anemia management is the patient-specific complication.
scenario_label: If dSDH-GIST phenotype confirmed (SDHB-IHC loss + biallelic SDHA inactivation locked in by SDHA IHC and germline panel)

intervention_label: Temozolomide on NCT05661643 (Asan, 200 mg/m² d1-5 q28d) or NCT03556384 (UCSD, 85 mg/m² d1-21 q28d, watch-for-readout); off-label generic TMZ with MGMT methylation as enrichment lever — contingency at first measurable recurrence
expected_benefit: Yebra 2022 (pmid:34426440) returned 2/5 PR and 100% disease control in a dSDH-GIST mini-cohort with paired PDX mechanism support — patient-derived models recapitulated parent-tumor biology and showed on-target alkylator damage. Flego 2024 (pmid:38132569) and Giger 2022 (pmid:36198483) identify MGMT promoter methylation as a candidate response biomarker enriched in ~24% of dSDH-GIST tumors. The exact binomial 95% CI on 2/5 PR runs roughly 5-85% — the point estimate is uninformative at that sample size; the load-bearing claim is mechanism coherence (PDX-to-clinic translation) rather than a precise effect estimate.

Myelosuppression, nausea, fatigue dominate the AE picture; class-known with published management algorithms
Ligon 2023 guadecitabine (0/9 across cohorts) is the cautionary mechanism-coherent precedent in this subset — hypomethylating-agent biology was right, clinical readout was a hard negative
TMZ PK after Roux-en-Y has not been formally studied — raises a tolerability question for low-dose continuous dosing
NCT05661643 is Korea-only (Asan); NCT03556384 is active-not-recruiting — if off-label US route is needed, MGMT methylation enrichment is the prior-auth lever
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: YES on trial-route; PARTIAL on off-label US route; matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (mature parent-drug safety, weak dSDH-specific efficacy estimate)
guideline_status: Off-guideline for GIST — neither NCCN nor ESMO lists TMZ for any GIST subtype. NCCN's trial-enrollment principle for off-guideline targeted therapy applies.

Critic's round-2 dissent on the risktaker's framing was sharp: 2/5 PR with no CI is not a 40% ORR estimate, and the rationale invoking 100% DCR at n=5 in an indolent natural-history setting brushes past the Ligon 2023 cautionary readout. Conservative's round-2 qualification on the concensusite pick added the MDS/AML chronic-exposure conversation — if the patient responds and stays on for years, the long-tail safety signal accrues on the natural-history timescale. The right framing is trial-route via NCT05661643 (recruiting, Korea-only — travel feasibility is the operational gate), watch for the NCT03556384 readout (UCSD, primary completion June 2025) before treating the case-series number as actionable, and order MGMT methylation on archival FFPE now so the prior-auth packet is ready if the off-label US path becomes the practical pivot at recurrence. Pre-specified cumulative-exposure re-evaluation at 9-12 months on therapy.

MGMT promoter methylation status on archival FFPE — order now to seed the prior-auth or trial-screening case at recurrence
Whether the patient can travel to Korea for the NCT05661643 enrollment vs whether off-label US TMZ is the operational pivot
Yebra 2022 protocol uses low-dose continuous 85 mg/m² d1-21; Asan trial uses 200 mg/m² d1-5 — schedule-by-schedule cytopenia / MDS risk differs
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate — Yebra 2022 2/5 PR (95% CI ~5-85%) is mechanism-coherent but uninformative at n=5; Ligon 2023 guadecitabine 0/9 is the cautionary precedent for mechanism-vs-clinic disconnect in this subset.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (myelosuppression, fatigue, nausea well-characterized; MDS/AML long-tail ~1% at cumulative exposure >6-12 months is the chronic signal)

scenario_label: If dSDH-GIST phenotype confirmed (SDHB-IHC loss or SDHx-mutation entry criterion for the temozolomide trials)

intervention_label: Pemigatinib on PEMIGIST (NCT07434843, DFCI single-site, Suzanne George) — contingency at first measurable recurrence
expected_benefit: Flynn 2025 AACR abstract CT215 (doi:10.1158/1538-7445.AM2025-CT215) showed tumor regression in a dSDH-GIST PDX model where sunitinib and regorafenib were essentially ineffective, with the mechanism rooted in CTCF-insulator disruption from genome-wide DNA hypermethylation → aberrant FGF3/4 transcription → autocrine/paracrine FGFR1 signaling. The cited bridge is rogaratinib (NCT04595747, n=24) at ORR 41.7% with 31-month median PFS — exact binomial 95% CI on 10/24 runs roughly 22-63%, so the point estimate is wide. NCT07434843 itself is n=24 single-arm phase 2 and will hit the same statistical wall on readout.
key_risks: FGFR-inhibitor class: serous retinal detachment in roughly 25% with cumulative exposure — requires baseline OCT + monthly OCT through first 6 months
Hyperphosphatemia approaching 60% all-grade — requires weekly phosphate during titration and a phosphate-binder management plan
Nail and mucosal toxicity drive dose holds; dermatology partner is part of the order set
AACR meeting abstract on a single PDX model is not peer-reviewed at full-paper resolution — the preclinical anchor pyramid is narrow
DFCI single-site — geography is a hard operational constraint
24-patient single-arm phase 2 will not generate long-tail safety dataset on the timescale a non-trial off-label decision would need
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: YES (recruiting); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (cleanest preclinical-to-clinic translation signal in dSDH-GIST so far, but evidence pyramid is shallow and AE class is monitoring-intensive); the advocate flagged that preferences are defaulted — a real elicitation must happen before this lands as a contingency
guideline_status: No NCCN or ESMO listing. Trial-enrollment principle is the only guideline framing.
rationale_summary: Risktaker placed pemigatinib at rank 1 (their highest-conviction trial-route bet); critic at rank 6 (trial-watch); concensusite at rank 5 (bundled with belzutifan and TMZ in the trial-route tier). Two formal round-2 dissents stacked: advocate dissent on preference-fit grounds (DFCI single-site is a logistics burden for a patient whose geography hasn't been elicited; AE counseling on serous retinal detachment and hyperphosphatemia is missing from the rationale) and critic dissent on evidence-quality grounds (one PDX in an AACR abstract plus a rogaratinib sister-drug readout at n=24 with wide binomial CI does not anchor a rank-1 pick — the rationale calls it the strongest preclinical-to-clinic translation and overstates what the evidence supports). Conservative's round-2 qualification on the same row added a chronic-toxicity conditional ask: if the patient reaches this pick, OCT baseline + monthly OCT through first 6 months and weekly phosphate during titration go in the order set. Status is considered_with_caveats per the two formal dissents (Hard Rule 3). Useful as the freshest mechanism story in the dossier with a clean clinical signal (rogaratinib 41.7% ORR) that the new trial may either replicate or fail to.
open_questions: NCT07434843 interim readout (trial opened April 2026; 24-patient design)
Whether the patient's geography supports DFCI enrollment
Whether rogaratinib (NCT04595747) data hold up at fuller publication
Whether AGS-25E or other FGFR programs open dSDH-GIST cohorts and dilute the single-site concentration
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate — rogaratinib NCT04595747 41.7% ORR at n=24 (95% CI ~22-63%) is the cited bridge; pemigatinib NCT07434843 itself is n=24 single-arm phase 2 with no readout yet.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (FGFR-class: serous retinal detachment ~25%, hyperphosphatemia ~60% all-grade, nail/mucosal AEs; monitoring-intensive class)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic and advocate dissented on evidence-pyramid narrowness and preference-fit; FGFR-class toxicity-as-monitoring-burden is the mechanism-adjacent concern.

overall: Freshest mechanism story in the dossier with the strongest preclinical-to-clinic signal so far, but the evidence pyramid is shallow and two personas dissented on rank-1 framing.
scenario_label: If dSDH-GIST phenotype confirmed (PEMIGIST entry phenotype is histologically confirmed SDH-deficient GIST)

intervention_label: Regorafenib 160 mg PO 3-on/1-off — 3L contingency at sunitinib progression
expected_benefit: Demetri 2013 GRID (pmid:23177515, RoB2:Low, n=199): PFS HR 0.27 (95% CI 0.19-0.39, p<0.0001), mPFS 4.8 vs 0.9 mo. Registration-grade 3L GIST. dSDH-GIST activity is by extrapolation — the Dedousis 2025 review (pmid:40045030) calls it 'modest, similar to KIT-mutant 3L' on qualitative narrative grounds, not a published subset analysis with a confidence interval.
key_risks: G3+ hypertension 23%, G3+ hand-foot skin reaction 20%, G3+ diarrhea 5% (GRID safety table) — dose modifications are the rule rather than the exception
Pre-treatment dermatology baseline and BP optimization save cycles 1-2 from becoming wasted
No prospective dSDH-GIST subgroup analysis exists — the 3L positioning rests on guideline extrapolation, not subset evidence
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: NO (FDA-approved 3L, not a trial); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (registration-grade RCT in a population that minimally represents dSDH-GIST)
guideline_status: NCCN GIST v1.2025 and ESMO 2022 both place regorafenib at 3L for advanced GIST. ESMO MCBS 3 for the registration setting; subset extrapolation to dSDH-GIST is not separately scored.
rationale_summary: Critic rank 4, concensusite rank 4. Advocate filed a round-2 dissent on preference-fit grounds: prefers_trials defaults to true, and putting regorafenib ahead of the trial-route options (rank 5 temozolomide, with belzutifan and pemigatinib bundled inside that pick) sequences a registration-grade TKI ahead of the patient's defaulted trial preference. By the time the patient progresses on sunitinib, the dSDH-GIST trial landscape will likely have moved and the right move at 3L should be a fresh trial-landscape review, not a rotation to regorafenib. Critic's round-2 qualification on the same pick added the evidence framing: GRID enrolled essentially no dSDH-GIST patients, and the Dedousis 2025 review's 'modest activity' claim is qualitative narrative. Status is considered_with_caveats per the formal advocate dissent. Defensible as a 3L contingency anchor because the alternatives are thinner, but at 3L the trial-route conversation should run alongside, not behind.
open_questions: At sunitinib progression, whether a fresh trial-landscape review surfaces a better third-line option than regorafenib (the trial portfolio is moving)
Whether ripretinib (Mavroeidis 2025: weakest dSDH-GIST evidence base of the three post-imatinib TKIs) belongs in the 4L slot or whether trial-route reaches it before that
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate in dSDH-GIST — GRID PFS HR 0.27 is registration-grade in KIT-mutant 3L; dSDH-subset activity is by extrapolation, no published subset CI.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ hypertension 23%, G3+ HFSR 20%, G3+ diarrhea 5%; dose modifications are the rule)

counter_productive_moa.description: Advocate dissent was preference-fit on sequencing against the trial-route, not on the mechanism.

overall: Registration-grade 3L anchor with weak dSDH-GIST subset evidence; sequencing against the trial-route at 3L is the live preference question.

intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID + temozolomide — late-line / post-trial-exhaustion contingency, trial-route only with hematology co-management (NOT off-label cash-pay default)
expected_benefit: Sulkowski 2018 (Nat Genet, pmid:30013182) and Sulkowski 2020 (Nature, pmid:32494005) build a tight mechanism case that SDH loss produces a BRCA-like phenotype at chromatin via succinate-driven KDM4B inhibition, sensitizing cells to PARP-trapping inhibitors. Singh 2023 (pmid:36151992) is a single-patient case report (multiply-relapsed dSDH-GIST + paraganglioma) with a durable clinical response on the combination. Mechanism is strong; human clinical evidence in dSDH-GIST is n=1.
key_risks: Overlapping cytopenias from PARP-trapping + alkylator are non-trivial in published combination data

OlympiA-style olaparib MDS/AML rates of approximately 1.2% rise sharply when the partner is itself genotoxic; TMZ carries its own ~1% MDS/AML long-tail at cumulative exposure beyond 6-12 months — the two together in a sustained-response scenario is exactly the chronic exposure where the MDS/AML signal compounds
No published combination safety dataset in dSDH-GIST to anchor a management algorithm
Off-label PARP-plus-alkylator outside a trial structure carries ~$17K/month cash-pay risk if appeal fails
Conservative's conditional veto: off-label use without trial structure, without baseline marrow assessment, and without a pre-specified cumulative-exposure stopping rule is not signable
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted prefers_trials: PARTIAL (no active dSDH-GIST trial of this combination; the only path is off-label or compassionate-use); matches efficacy-toxicity weight 0.65: NO at the off-label cash-pay default; the conservative's bounded framing ('late-line, trial-route only, with hematology co-management, with a pre-specified cumulative-exposure stopping rule') is the only preference-aligned use
guideline_status: Not NCCN-listed for any GIST subtype. PARP-plus-alkylator in dSDH-GIST is mechanism-supported but has no guideline category.
rationale_summary: Risktaker rank 4 (their own characterization: 'the weakest in this position'). Conservative filed a round-2 dissent + conditional veto on toxicity and evidence-quality grounds: the n=1 Singh 2023 case report cannot adjudicate the combination's chronic-toxicity profile, the MDS/AML signal compounds across PARP + alkylator in sustained-response scenarios, and off-label cash-pay use without baseline marrow assessment and a pre-specified cumulative-exposure stopping rule is not signable. Critic filed a round-2 qualification on the same row: the mechanism work is real and tight, but the n=1 caveat must travel forward so the row is not cited as 'durable response in dSDH-GIST' downstream. Status is considered_with_caveats with the conservative veto OVERRIDDEN to the bounded framing: late-line, post-trial-exhaustion only, trial-route or compassionate-use only, hematology co-management with baseline marrow assessment, pre-specified 9-12 month cumulative-exposure re-evaluation. In the off-label cash-pay default framing the conservative veto stands. The row is on the page so the reader can see the mechanism story was considered with the explicit guardrails the veto requires.
open_questions: Whether an investigator-initiated trial of PARP + TMZ in dSDH-GIST opens (the natural sponsor is the NIH wt-GIST clinic or DFCI; nothing currently registered)
Whether the patient's marrow reserve at the time of late-line reach-for is adequate for the combination
Whether the Singh 2023 single case represents a real signal or a regression to the mean of dSDH-GIST natural-history indolence
likelihood_of_effect: Low for population-level effect — Singh 2023 is n=1; Sulkowski mechanism work is robust at chromatin level but no replicated clinical readout in dSDH-GIST.
toxicity_burden: High (overlapping PARP + alkylator cytopenias; cumulative MDS/AML risk on sustained exposure; no published combination safety dataset in dSDH-GIST)

counter_productive_moa.description: Conservative veto stood on chronic-toxicity-as-mechanism: PARP + alkylator MDS/AML compounding in sustained-response scenarios is the mechanism-level risk to durable use.

overall: Mechanism-strong, evidence-thin late-line contingency — acceptable only in bounded trial-route or hematology-comanaged framing; off-label cash-pay default is not signable.
scenario_label: If dSDH-GIST phenotype confirmed AND prior dSDH-targeted contingencies (sunitinib, belzutifan / TMZ / pemigatinib trials, regorafenib) have been exhausted

intervention_label: Adjuvant imatinib — NOT RECOMMENDED in dSDH-GIST (logged on the record so the no-imatinib decision is documented and not re-litigated)
expected_benefit: None in this molecular subset. Boikos 2016 (pmid:27011036): 1/49 (2%) PR in dSDH-GIST on imatinib. The Z9001 / SSGXVIII / PERSIST-5 adjuvant evidence base (RFS HR 0.35 in Z9001; RFS HR 0.46 and OS HR 0.45 in SSGXVIII; PERSIST-5 5-yr RFS 90%) was built in KIT-mutant high-risk disease with dSDH-GIST structurally absent — the subset was not a recognized molecular entity at the time those trials accrued, and PERSIST-5 separated out the imatinib-insensitive genotypes and showed they recur on or off treatment.
key_risks: 3-year exposure AE profile: G2+ edema ~30%, fatigue ~50%, plus unquantified long-tail of cardiac and hepatic monitoring burden — not a defensible tradeoff at a 2% PR rate
Burns screening eligibility for several recurrence-contingency trials (most require measurable disease and deprioritize prior-systemic-therapy patients)
'GIST equals imatinib' is the reflex the surgical team and any downstream community oncologist may reach for — the documented veto in the structured output is the insurance against that failure mode
preference_alignment: matches user's defaulted efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: NO (no efficacy signal to lean on for an adjuvant regimen in this subset; toxicity side dominates by default); matches prefers_trials: NO
guideline_status: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 explicitly recommends AGAINST adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST. NCCN GIST v1.2025 lists imatinib as standard adjuvant only for KIT-mutant high-risk GIST; KIT/PDGFRA-WT subtypes including dSDH-GIST are flagged as imatinib-insensitive.
rationale_summary: The advocate listed adjuvant imatinib at rank 6 in their own picks specifically to mark it NOT-recommended and put the veto on the record. Conservative's round-2 critique amplified the veto explicitly: 'any subsequent recommendation in this case that initiates adjuvant imatinib (or any adjuvant systemic therapy) in this NED dSDH-GIST patient draws an unconditional veto from me.' Critic's round-2 endorsement of the advocate's NOT-recommended call adds the evidence-quality concurrence: 'Boikos 1/49 (2%) PR is the published anchor, ESMO 2022 is explicit, and PERSIST-5 separating out the imatinib-insensitive genotypes is the cleanest single demonstration that dSDH-GIST belongs in the imatinib-insensitive class.' All five personas reject this intervention. Status is not_recommended. Row kept on the page so the reader can see what was considered and rejected; the most likely failure mode downstream is the reflex 'GIST equals imatinib' reach, and a documented veto is the cheapest insurance.
open_questions: Whether the surgical team will raise this on the post-op note — the chart note should pre-emptively cite ESMO 2022 and Boikos 2016 so the decision is documented and does not get re-litigated
likelihood_of_effect: None in dSDH-GIST — Boikos 2016 1/49 (2%) PR on imatinib; adjuvant trials structurally excluded this subset.
toxicity_burden: High (3-year exposure: G2+ edema ~30%, fatigue ~50%, hepatic / cardiac monitoring burden) measured against a 2% PR rate — not a defensible tradeoff.

counter_productive_moa.description: Both vetoes stood on mechanism + toxicity: imatinib insensitivity in dSDH-GIST plus chronic AE burden at the 2% PR floor; PERSIST-5 confirmed imatinib-insensitive genotypes recur regardless of treatment.

overall: Logged as NOT RECOMMENDED so the reflex 'GIST equals imatinib' reach is documented and rejected on the record — every persona vetoed in concept.
